sentence_of_record: On R2's B0 MMLU_PRO_LB member root (draw 5a3e756 TRAIN; qwen3 512-slice; sepBar 0.0145; 300 reps), the declared 14-category MMLU-Pro partition, stratified-subsampled to G12's depth-1 site sizes, is CERTIFIED by its own site null at n 486 (PS1, 5 of 5 subsamples) and n 441 (PS2, 5 of 5), and descriptively at n 264 (5 of 5); k_d 0 of 300 everywhere (p 1/301); C0 comparable 15 of 15. ["The site-null certificate is not size-limited at G12's depth-1 sizes for structure of the declared 14-category strength: its bar there (null p95 about 0.05-0.06) is cleared with margin. G12's 0 of 60 is therefore NOT explained by n alone. The tree's data-driven depth-1 splits are less separated than the declared level at the same n, and 13 of G12's 14 TOP splits fall below their own null median." Mandatory caveats beside it: (i) NOT k-matched: 14 groups vs 2. (ii) NOT population-matched: all categories vs within one anchor; CERT-POSITIVE-CONTROL's PC3, descriptive, found 0 of 14 declared src partitions certified inside anchors, src geometry unknown. (iii) Nothing is shown about whether certifiable 2-way structure EXISTS inside an anchor, nor about the certificate's power for it there. F-TAX N-1 and F2 stand.]

plain_description.what: Takes the 14 declared MMLU-Pro subject categories and shrinks them to the small sample sizes of the tree's first-level splits (486, 441 and 264 questions). It then checks whether the split certificate, which compares against random reshuffles, still certifies them. No judge calls.
plain_description.why: An earlier test certified 0 of 60 first-level tree splits. This test checks whether that happened only because the samples were too small for the certificate.
plain_description.information: If the known-real categories fail at these sizes, the earlier zero means nothing. If they pass, the tree's splits really are weaker. Result: the declared categories were certified in 5 of 5 subsamples at every size. So the certificate is not limited by sample size here, and the tree's own first-level splits are less separated than the declared categories. Caveat: this compares 14 groups against 2-way splits, on different populations.
